stem_book: A solid sphere is given an angular velocity ω and kept (with no linear velocity) on a rough fixed inclined plane; as shown in the figure the spin is clockwise, the incline rising to the right, so the contact point slides DOWN the incline. Choose the correct statement(s). (a) If μ = tanθ then sphere will be in linear equilibrium for some time and after that pure rolling down the plane will start. (b) If μ = tanθ then sphere will move up the plane and frictional force acting all the time will be 2mg sinθ (c) If μ = tanθ/2 there will never be pure rolling (consider inclined plane to be long enough) (d) If incline plane is not fixed and it is on smooth horizontal surface then linear momentum of the system (wedge and sphere) can be conserved in horizontal direction.
key: d horizontal momentum of wedge + sphere is conserved
reason: printed key d only (true for the opposite spin, which the manifest stem assumed); the figure's spin is clockwise (bottom slides down-slope) ⇒ μ = tanθ gives kinetic friction mg sinθ up-slope = mg sinθ down ⇒ linear equilibrium until ω = 0, then pure rolling down (needs only μ ≥ (2/7)tanθ) ⇒ (a) also true
work: clockwise ω: f = μmg cosθ = mg sinθ up-slope ⇒ a_cm = 0, α = 5g sinθ/(2R) kills ω; then rolls down with f = (2/7)mg sinθ < μN ⇒ (a); no external horizontal force on wedge+sphere ⇒ (d); (c): slip speed ω₀R − (3/4)g sinθ t → 0 ⇒ rolls ⇒ false
